text:
marta: Seeing a spike of image pull failures on inference nodes in us-east-2. `docker pull` against our private ECR times out or gets TLS resets. Affected nodes are on subnet prod-gpu-a. Anyone else?
infra-bot: [alert] ENI detach/attach on interface endpoint ep-ecr-xyz (subnet prod-gpu-a) at 2026-02-12T14:20:03Z; health=unhealthy -> healthy
kevin: same here. Looks like some requests are being routed out via the Transit Gateway/NAT instead of the interface endpoint IP. Packet capture shows SYN -> SYN/ACK to EP IP then immediate RST from outside path.
jules: can you paste a quick curl with --resolve so we see handshake? e.g. `curl -v --resolve "012345678901.dkr.ecr.us-east-2.amazonaws.com:443:10.0.5.12" https://012345678901.dkr.ecr.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v2/`
marta: ran that from a node, output: TLS handshake, then `Connection reset by peer`. tcpdump on node: src=10.0.5.21 dst=10.0.5.12, reply came back from TGW path with src=18.23.45.67 and replaced dst -> node, so return path is asymmetric.
samir: suspect route table association change for the EP subnet. If the subnet hosting the endpoint got associated to an RT that propagates to TGW, the endpoint ENI return traffic can be misrouted. Can you run `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-abcdef`?
kevin: ran it, output snippet: ```
{
  "RouteTables": [
    {
      "RouteTableId": "rtb-0abc",
      "Associations": [ { "SubnetId": "subnet-abcdef" } ],
      "Routes": [ { "DestinationCidrBlock": "0.0.0.0/0", "GatewayId": "tgw-05f" } ]
    }
  ]
}
```
jules: ouch. That subnet is pointing 0.0.0.0/0 at the TGW. Interface endpoints expect local routing back to the VPC/ENI. TGW propagation will steer replies out. Also check the ENI owner and Source/Dest check: `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --network-interface-ids eni-0aa`
marta: ENI looks owned by `com.amazonaws.vpce`, src/dst check=enabled. Automation changed subnet->route-table association during a remediation run.
kevin: fix path: re-associate subnet to the VPC-local route table used for endpoints (rtb-local-ep), then clear conntrack on nodes so stale NAT translations are gone. Commands we ran: `aws ec2 associate-route-table --subnet-id subnet-abcdef --route-table-id rtb-local-ep` then on nodes `sudo conntrack -F` (or `sudo conntrack -D -s <node-ip>` when you want selective flush).
marta: after re-assoc + conntrack flush, image pulls recovered within ~20s. Monitoring shows no more ENI flaps.
samir: root cause: infra automation mistakenly moved association to RT that propagates to TGW during a global RT cleanup; that created asymmetric return path so endpoint replies went via TGW/NAT and were dropped/reset.
oncall: created ticket INF-2345 to add a terraform guardrail and an automated check in pr-lint that flags changing route-table associations on subnets hosting interface endpoints.
jules: recommend also adding a metric alert on interface endpoint health + ECR pull error rate to catch earlier (threshold 5% over 1m).
marta: thanks all :thumbsup: will follow up in the infra runbook with the remediation steps and add the PR lint rule.
kevin: quick note for posterity: if you see ECR pulls succeed sometimes and fail other times, check for asymmetric routing (TGW/NAT) and stale conntrack before escalating to AWS support.
marta: closing the thread, marking nodes healthy. :party_parrot:
